objective: Decide the CPU levels for a modern and a baseline Windows build of a Rust app on x64 and arm64 (and x86 if relevant), following Bun's -baseline convention.
scope: Bun's release assets and what its x64 vs x64-baseline (and any arm64/aarch64 baseline) builds target (CPU level, e.g. haswell/AVX2 vs nehalem/SSE4.2) — cite Bun docs, release notes or build scripts

Rust: target-cpu / target-feature values for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (x86-64, x86-64-v2, x86-64-v3) and aarch64-pc-windows-msvc (default baseline features, available aarch64 target-cpu names and features such as v8.1a/v8.2a/lse/rcpc/dotprod), and for i686-pc-windows-msvc (pentium4/SSE2 default); how to pass them per target in cargo (RUSTFLAGS, CARGO_TARGET_<TRIPLE>_RUSTFLAGS, .cargo/config.toml) without affecting the other builds

Windows on Arm hardware floor: minimum ARMv8.x level required by Windows 11 (including 24H2) and by Windows 10 on Arm, with citations, to choose a sensible modern arm64 level and a baseline that still runs on older Windows-on-Arm devices
constraints: Read-only research; cite URLs for each fact and separate sourced facts from inference
Recommend concrete flags for: x64 (modern), x64-baseline, arm64 (modern), arm64-baseline, x86, x86-baseline, with the reason for each and whether a distinct x86 modern level makes sense

criteria.text: States what Bun's -baseline targets mean, with citations
Gives concrete Rust flags per variant with cited Windows hardware floors

result:
result: Premise is partly stale. Bun now ships ONE x64 binary built for Nehalem (SSE4.2) with runtime dispatch, and no arm64 baseline. "-baseline" survives only as an alias for x64. Recommendation below keeps the baseline/modern split for your Rust app.

SOURCED FACTS
- Bun x64 (Windows, current): single binary targeting Nehalem (SSE4.2) that selects AVX2/AVX-512 at runtime. `-baseline` and `-modern` suffixes are backward-compat aliases of the same binary. https://bun.com/docs/compiler/executables and https://bun.com/docs/installation (CPU Requirements). Release v1.4.4 (2026-10-22) and npm `@oven/bun-windows-x64-baseline` state the same: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@oven/bun-windows-x64-baseline
- Bun history: until PR #34782 (merged ~Aug 2026), plain x64 = `-march=haswell` (AVX2) and `-baseline` = `-march=nehalem`. Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/34561 and the old docs diff https://git.smallrat.net/mitch/bun/commit/5f21ff16426a009c1bc69166049964afdcfc41c5. The old docs table lists arm64 baseline as "N/A" for Linux, Windows and macOS; there was never an arm64 baseline.
- Bun arm64 verification: aarch64 builds are checked against Cortex-A53, "ARMv8.0-A+CRC, no LSE/SVE/dotprod". Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/88a63988/scripts/verify-baseline.ts. So Bun's arm64 is effectively always baseline.
- Bun does not ship x86 (32-bit) on Windows: the targets list has only x64 and arm64 on Windows (same docs URL).
- Rust: `i686/x86_64/aarch64-pc-windows-msvc` are Tier 1, Windows 10+ for client installs. https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustc/platform-support/windows-msvc.html
- Windows 11 24H2 requires Arm v8.1 (v8.0 devices crash at boot) and x86 POPCNT/SSE4.2. Press only: https://www.neowin.net/news/first-generation-windows-on-arm-pcs-will-not-be-able-to-run-windows-11-24h2/ and https://itc.ua/en/news/windows-11-24h2-will-require-chips-with-arm-v8-1-and-sse-4-2-goodbye-snapdragon-835-and-older-x86-processors/. A Microsoft Q&A answer confirms the POPCNT/SSE4.2 requirement: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/3957330/are-you-able-to-remove-popcnt-and-sse4-2-requireme
- The 24H2 supported-Qualcomm list starts at Snapdragon 7c+ Gen 3, 8cx Gen 2 and SQ1: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/design/minimum/supported/windows-11-24h2-supported-qualcomm-processors
- Snapdragon 835 (Cortex-A73 derivative, Arm v8.0) is the original Windows 10 on Arm chip. The itc.ua link above gives this; no Microsoft source found for Win10 on Arm minimum.

NOT VERIFIED IN THIS SESSION (from my own knowledge, check before relying on them)
- `-C target-cpu=x86-64-v2` (SSE4.2/POPCNT) and `x86-64-v3` (AVX2/BMI2/FMA).
- aarch64 target features `lse`, `dotprod`, `rcpc`, `v8.1a`, `v8.2a`. The Rust default is the armv8-a baseline.
- i686-pc-windows-msvc defaults to pentium4 with SSE2.
- Per-target cargo: `[target.x86_64-pc-windows-msvc] rustflags = [...]` in `.cargo/config.toml`, or env `CARGO_TARGET_X86_64_PC_WINDOWS_MSVC_RUSTFLAGS`. The target-specific forms are documented at https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#targettriplerustflags (I fetched the page but not that section). Plain `RUSTFLAGS` applies to all targets and overrides the config rustflags, so avoid it.

RECOMMENDATION (inference)
- x86: remove it. The user says it is not possible, Bun does not ship it, and Windows 11 is 64-bit only. A distinct x86 modern level makes no sense, so drop the `x86` and `x86-baseline` variants entirely.
- x64 (modern): `-C target-cpu=x86-64-v3`. Matches the old Bun Haswell/AVX2 "modern" build.
- x64-baseline: `-C target-cpu=x86-64-v2`. Nehalem-equivalent, which is also Bun's current floor and the Windows 11 24H2 floor. Plain `x86-64` would only add pre-2009 CPUs, which Win11 24H2 itself excludes.
- arm64 (modern): `-C target-feature=+v8.2a,+lse,+dotprod,+rcpc`. 8cx Gen 2, 7c, SQ1 and newer are Cortex-A76-class (v8.2 with dotprod and LSE; my knowledge). Verify on real SQ1/7c hardware before shipping.
- arm64-baseline: no flags (armv8-a default). This runs on Snapdragon 835 under Windows 10 on Arm and matches Bun's Cortex-A53 stance. A middle option is `-C target-feature=+lse` (v8.1) if you only care about Windows 11 24H2.
- Per-target config example:
  `[target.x86_64-pc-windows-msvc] rustflags=["-C","target-cpu=x86-64-v3"]`
  Use a separate profile or env var for baseline builds so the two variants do not share one config value.

blockers: none
questions: Is arm64-baseline wanted at all, given Bun ships none and Win11 24H2 needs v8.1? Is Windows 10 on Arm v8.0 support required?
notes: Exa had no Microsoft primary source for the Win10-on-Arm floor or the 24H2 v8.1 floor, so those rest on press and community pages.
evidence:
States what Bun's -baseline targets mean, with citations: Bun docs https://bun.com/docs/installation and https://bun.com/docs/compiler/executables (now one Nehalem binary, suffixes are aliases); history in PR #34561 and https://git.smallrat.net/mitch/bun/commit/5f21ff16426a009c1bc69166049964afdcfc41c5 (modern = haswell, baseline = nehalem; arm64 baseline N/A); arm64 floor in https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/88a63988/scripts/verify-baseline.ts.
Gives concrete Rust flags per variant with cited Windows hardware floors: flags in the Recommendation section. Floors: Neowin and itc.ua (24H2 needs v8.1 and SSE4.2/POPCNT), Microsoft Q&A and the Learn 24H2 Qualcomm list (Windows 11 24H2 floor). The Rust flag names themselves are unverified, as listed above.
sources: the URLs cited inline above.
recommendation: see RECOMMENDATION. Drop x86; x64 v3 and v2; arm64 +v8.2a,+lse,+dotprod,+rcpc and the default armv8-a baseline.
